question: A 22-year-old presents with severe sore throat, exudative tonsillitis, marked cervical lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly. You are considering prescribing an antibiotic. Which of the following is the most important concern?

answers.text: Risk of antibiotic resistance if a broad-spectrum agent is used

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Antibiotic stewardship is important, but in this clinical scenario the specific danger is not resistance — it is the life-threatening rash triggered by amoxicillin in EBV-related infectious mononucleosis.

answers.text: Prescribing amoxicillin (or ampicillin) in a patient likely to have infectious mononucleosis will cause a widespread maculopapular rash

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Splenomegaly, exudative tonsillitis, and marked lymphadenopathy in a young adult strongly suggest infectious mononucleosis (EBV). Amoxicillin or ampicillin given in this setting triggers a widespread maculopapular rash in ~90% of cases. A monospot test or Paul-Bunnell test must be performed first.

answers.text: The patient may require urgent tonsillectomy as the first-line treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tonsillectomy is not first-line for acute EBV tonsillitis. The urgent concern is avoiding amoxicillin/ampicillin, which triggers a severe drug-virus interaction rash.

answers.text: Penicillin V is ineffective against Group A Streptococcus in adults over 18

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Penicillin V remains effective against Group A Streptococcus at all ages. The clinical scenario here points to EBV, and the specific hazard is the amoxicillin/ampicillin rash, not penicillin V failure.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the clinical trap: amoxicillin (or ampicillin) given during EBV infectious mononucleosis triggers a severe widespread rash. Always check for EBV in atypical tonsillitis presentations before prescribing.
Excellent. The amoxicillin-in-EBV trap is a classic ENT danger: splenomegaly + exudative tonsillitis in a young adult = exclude EBV before giving any aminopenicillin.
